sentence: This project studies how physical activity and self-regulation are linked to loss of control eating in children from late childhood to adolescence.
This project studies how oligodendrocytes, which are glial cells of the central nervous system, form myelin on select axons during development.
This project tries to make T cell immunotherapies work better against cancer by removing an inhibitory factor from the T cells.
This project builds ways to measure membrane tension in live cells using optical tweezers and tension gauges made from mechanosensitive ion channels.
This project builds computational tools that find genes and regulatory elements responsible for specific organismal traits.
This project compares natural dormancy in a genetic model with a 3D bone model of breast cancer dormancy to find genes that control it.
This project studies how an antiviral enzyme restricts Epstein-Barr virus infection and how the viral ribonucleotide reductase blocks it.
This project tries to grow a rat liver inside a mouse embryo by knocking out mouse liver genes and injecting donor rat stem cells.
This project studies how signaling through G protein-coupled receptors is organized and regulated in the cell.
This project studies how linear and nonlinear mechanical forces regulate cellular metabolism.
This project builds a computer tool that uses digital otoscopy and machine learning to help diagnose ear abnormalities.
This project tries to find out how T cells cause oral mucosal adverse events from immune checkpoint blockade.
This project studies how platelets contribute to alcohol-associated liver disease.
This project studies how human tumors treated with an oncolytic virus change, using immunologic, biologic and imaging analyses.
This project tries to find out how changing mechanical load on the heart affects the transverse tubules of heart muscle membrane.
This project studies why gastrointestinal stromal tumor becomes aggressive and tries to find molecular biomarkers that predict recurrence risk.
This project tries to find out how time-restricted feeding of a high-fat diet stops obesity from driving breast cancer in mice.
This project builds reagents and methods to measure phosphorylation changes on proteins in bacteria and other cells.
This project tries to find out what controls enhancer activity during pluripotency and pre-implantation development.
This project provides brain imaging, including magnetic resonance imaging and positron emission tomography scans, for a study of healthy aging and senile dementia.
